label: PF Backlog 651
title: Backlog execution trail: ordered stage ledger + tests/usage/cost report + completion guard

decisions.note: HIL requested the execution trail; design sha b1552bcee88b: 4 blockers actioned (failure sink, atomic lock, stage ownership, diff scoping), 5 majors actioned; 0 pending.

BI-PF-1481 implementation lives in core/execution_trail.py (governance-allowlisted control-plane evidence), not a thin scripts adapter; AC/docs corrected; language-rule allowlist is the approved exception.
Final sha d3067222ee09: 2 blockers accepted (owner amendment: core allowlisted implementation; presence + key-pair order), 8 majors accepted as documented residual hardening.
f5f706606b49: accepted a 5th review to fix the CI execution-trail base fallback; churn reviewed and accepted.

brief.problem: Backlog execution is ad hoc: no single ordered trail of gates/tests/decisions/PR/usage/cost per item.
brief.what_adds: A registered append-only execution-trail store, a show/finalize CLI, automatic writes from the gate tools, and a completion gate.
brief.why_now: EDP-10/1480 showed the process is only as good as the visible trail; every session/LLM must follow it.
brief.success: Every completion has an ordered trail with tests/results/time/PR/usage and a final next-item table; missing stages fail precheck.

objective: Give every backlog item one ordered, append-only execution trail from Gate 0 to completion, written automatically by the gate tools, with a show CLI (gates, tests, usage, final table, next item) and a completion gate that fails missing/out-of-order stages.
acceptance_criteria: A registered store engineering/trails/<ITEM>.json (owner core/execution_trail.py, a thin adapter to scripts/dev/execution_trail.py) records append-only events {seq, at, stage, actor, status, summary, refs, tests, usage, duration_ms} for planning, gate0, design_review, gate1, implementation, code_review, diff_review, gate2, tests, precheck, pr, merge, delivery, completion; seq is monotonic under a per-item lock.

python -m core.execution_trail show --item <ID> renders the ordered trail, the Gate 1.5/2.5 decision tables + recommendations (from the review evidence), the tests table (command/result/duration), usage totals (input/output/cached tokens; 'not captured' when unavailable), and the final completion table with PR/merge, total time, next backlog item.

The gate tools write the trail automatically: gate0_check, architect_review (design/diff + provider usage), gate_decide, precheck (tests/precheck timings), core.backlog.set_delivery and set_status(completed); no manual record is needed for a normal item.

scripts/dev/execution_trail_check.py runs as a POST-precheck gate (after tests/precheck events are written) and fails a completion in the diff when the pre-merge stages planning/gate0/design_review/gate1/implementation/code_review/diff_review/gate2/tests/precheck are missing or out of order, or when a DEFERRED finding has no follow-up BI-... id; pr/merge/delivery/completion are post-merge and shown when present. A trail write failure emits a structured execution_trail_write_failed event and the completion gate fails; the check is self-tested and wired into precheck + ci-cd-gates.
out_of_scope: Fabricating coding-session token counts/cost (only captured sources are recorded).
Retroactively backfilling every legacy item (completion gate applies to items in the diff).
Changing the gate order or review framework.
approach: Add scripts/dev/execution_trail.py + a thin core/execution_trail.py adapter (allowlisted) and scripts/dev/execution_trail_check.py. Wire gate0_check (planning/gate0), architect_review (design/diff + provider usage), gate_decisions (gate1/2), precheck (implementation/code_review/tests/precheck, POST gate), core.backlog.set_delivery/set_status (delivery/completion). The show CLI renders stages, Gate 1.5/2.5 tables, tests, usage and the final/next table. Write failures are logged (execution_trail_write_failed) and the POST completion gate fails missing/out-of-order stages or DEFERRED without a follow-up id.

prior_decisions: Gate 0/1.5/1/2.5/2 are binding (docs/REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md); evidence is per SHA; review churn is bounded (BI-PF-1480).
Backlog is the work SSOT and is written only through core.backlog (API); evidence attaches to the owner store and references item_id.
Precheck fast runs scoped tests/gates; --full/CI adds the wide set. Timings are printed but not persisted per item.
core.audit_trail.py / core.backlog.py set the precedent for Python control-plane/evidence tooling (not customer runtime).
existing_path: core/backlog.py: set_status/set_delivery/update; item decisions/evidence/verification/delivery; execution.usage from workers.
scripts/dev/gate0_check.py, architect_review.py, gate_decide.py/gate_decisions.py, precheck.py, gate2_completion_check.py, review_churn_check.py.
assumptions: A trail is a per-item append-only JSON store; stages are recorded by the tools, not hand-written.
Completion (status completed) is the enforcement point for the pre-merge stages; merge/delivery/completion events are appended after the PR/merge.

Provider usage (input/output/cached tokens) is available from the review API response; coding-session tokens are only available if the harness/worker writes item.execution.usage, otherwise shown as 'not captured'.
DEFERRED dispositions must name a follow-up item id in their note; the completion gate checks it when present.
core/execution_trail.py is a thin adapter to the tooling implementation (allowlisted in config/language-rule.json); python -m core.execution_trail works.
The completion gate enforces the pre-merge stages because the item is marked completed before the PR/merge; pr/merge/delivery/completion events are appended after merge and shown when present.
Trail write failures are logged as structured events; the POST-precheck completion gate is the fail-closed enforcement.
divergences: The trail is a new evidence store (not a backlog field) to keep the item lean and the history append-only; it references item_id.
The trail is written by the gate tools (automatic) and checked at completion (fail closed), rather than relying on manual summaries.
The completion gate runs as a POST gate so it sees the tests/precheck events written by the same precheck run.

impact_review.evidence: No HTTP surface: core CLI + gate tooling; no route/tenant input.

evidence: A registered store engineering/trails/<ITEM>.json (owner core/execution_trail.py) records append-only events {seq, at, stage, actor, status, summary, refs, tests, usage, duration_ms} for planning, gate0, design_review, gate1, implementation, code_review, diff_review, gate2, tests, precheck, pr, merge, delivery, completion.

python -m core.execution_trail show --item <ID> renders the ordered trail, the Gate 1.5/2.5 decision tables + recommendations (from the review evidence), the tests table (command/result/duration), usage totals (input/output/cached tokens; 'not captured' when unavailable), and the final completion table with PR/merge, total time, next backlog item.

The gate tools write the trail automatically: gate0_check, architect_review (design/diff + provider usage), gate_decide, precheck (tests/precheck timings), core.backlog.set_delivery and set_status(completed); no manual record is needed for a normal item.

scripts/dev/execution_trail_check.py (precheck fast) fails a completion in the diff when required stages are missing or out of order, or when a DEFERRED finding has no follow-up item; the check is self-tested and wired into precheck + ci-cd-gates.

impact_review.evidence: Python control-plane/evidence tooling (core/execution_trail.py + scripts/dev), not customer runtime; language_rule_review will be run.
Extends the existing gate tools (gate0, architect_review, gate_decide, precheck, backlog) and reuses the evidence/decisions stores; no second backlog or review engine.
POST-precheck execution_trail_check: pre-merge stages in order + DEFERRED follow-up ids; a write failure is logged and the gate fails.
Review usage is captured; session usage is shown as not captured unless item.execution.usage exists. No fabricated cost.
Trail writes are best-effort in the tools; the completion gate is the enforcement. Rollback is a revert; trail files are append-only evidence.

risks: A trail write failure must not fail a gate; the completion gate catches a missing trail.
Concurrent sessions: the trail uses a per-item lock and append-only events.
Legacy items have no trail; the gate only enforces completions in the diff.
Session token/cost may be unavailable; the report says so instead of guessing.
rollback: Revert the tooling/config commit; trail files are append-only evidence and can remain.

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=db39a08040f2
BLOCKER:
  - AC/owner mismatch: AC requires `owner core/execution_trail.py` and `python -m core.execution_trail show`, but the design ships `scripts/dev/execution_trail.py`; `python -m core.execution_trail` cannot resolve. AC 1 and 2 are not met as written.
  - Silent best-effort hook: a failed trail write drops required evidence (e.g. `delivery`/`completion`) with no failure signal, yet the completion gate then fails the item — gate outcome becomes dependent on an unlogged side channel rather than a checked contract.
MAJOR:
  - Dependency inversion: `core/backlog.py` (shipped core) invoking a `scripts/dev` hook makes core depend on dev tooling; failure coupling and reload/ordering semantics are undefined.
  - No stated invariant for `seq` uniqueness/monotonicity across concurrent writers; a per-item lock alone does not prove ordering, and no concurrency/append test is listed.
  - Completion gate enforces only a subset (`gate0/design_review/gate1/diff_review/gate2/tests`); `planning`, `pr`, `merge`, `delivery`, `completion`, `implementation`, `code_review`, `precheck` are in the AC stage list but unenforced — out-of-order or absent late stages pass the gate.
  - No observability plan for trail writes (metric/log/counter on append failure, hook miss, lock contention); without it, "best-effort" is undiagnosable in production runs.
  - Test scope covers only `test_execution_trail.py` happy path; recurring review findings call out missing coverage for render/disposition helpers and check failure paths (`DEFERRED` without follow-up, out-of-order detection).
  - `architect_review.render_gate_view` reuse appears to reach into private helpers (`_render_review`, `_item_dispositions`) — cross-module reuse of private API is a maintainability and contract risk.
MINOR:
  - No redaction/retention policy for `refs`/`summary`/token usage persisted in the durable trail store (checklist items 9, 4).
  - Append-only JSON has no size bound, rotation, or compaction; long-lived items grow unbounded.
  - Usage "not captured" vs. zero semantics not defined for partially captured sessions (mixed sources in one trail).
  - "next backlog item" and "total time" in the final table have no defined behavior for partial/legacy/incomplete trails.
  - Rollback leaves `config/store-registry.json` and `config/ci-cd-gates.json` referencing a removed tool — restore path for config not stated.
NIT:
  - Checklist guardrail questions (backup/restore before any destructive step, SPOF/alert lead-time, needs_api) are not explicitly answered in the design text even though the design guardrails require it.
  - Naming: item in_scope says `scripts/dev/*` while AC says `core/*`; pick one and align all three of AC, in_scope, and affected_files.
SUMMARY:
  - Solid direction: append-only registered store, tool-written evidence, and a fail-able completion check are the right shape, and reuse of `architect_review` render + store registry is good.
  - Top risks: (1) AC module path/owner is contradicted by the design, (2) best-effort writes silently corrupt gate evidence with no observability, (3) the completion gate enforces only ~6 of 14 mandated stages, so ordering integrity is not actually guaranteed.
  - Must resolve the owner mismatch and define the write-failure contract (log/metric + gate behavior) before Gate 1.5.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=b1552bcee88b
BLOCKER:
  - AC/design conflict: a trail *write failure* cannot be recorded as an `execution_trail_write_failed` event inside the same failing trail; no alternate durable sink (log/metric/separate store) is specified, so the failure signal and the gate verdict can silently diverge.
  - Append-only atomicity unspecified: no temp-write+rename/fsync or lock mechanism (flock? lockfile?) is stated for read-modify-write seq allocation; a crash or two writers can duplicate or skip seq, violating the monotonic-seq AC with no test named for it.
  - AC says `precheck` writes tests/precheck timings only, but the design assigns `precheck` to also write implementation/code_review events; stage ownership is ambiguous and the out-of-order check cannot be trusted until one source of truth exists.
  - `scripts/dev/execution_trail_check.py`'s "in the diff" scoping for which completions to enforce is undefined (git range? changed files?); without a deterministic rule the gate can be bypassed or fail unrelated legacy items.
MAJOR:
  - DEFERRED-follow-up validation only regexes a `BI-...` id; it does not verify the id exists/open in the backlog, so a bogus token satisfies the gate (integrity hole).
  - Store ownership is split (`core/execution_trail.py` adapter owner vs `scripts/dev/execution_trail.py` implementation) with no statement of which is canonical for schema evolution, imports, or versioning — duplicate-surface drift risk.
  - AC names `gate_decide` while files/design say `gate_decisions.py`; wiring list must reconcile tool names or the auto-write path silently misses a stage.
  - No test named for the ordering/missing-stage check itself across every required stage, nor for seq-under-concurrency; only a generic `test_execution_trail.py` is listed — gates need fail-able tests (guardrail 6/5).
  - Observability: only a failure log event is mentioned; no counter/log for trail write latency, lock contention, or skipped stages, so production diagnosing relies on reading JSON files.
MINOR:
  - No secret/redaction policy for `summary`/`refs`/`usage` payload fields written by gate tools into a long-lived store.
  - Rollback says trail files "can remain" but no retention/compaction/size bound is defined for append-only per-item JSON growth.
  - Language rule: `core/execution_trail.py` is new shipped Python; justified only as a thin allowlisted adapter — the "thinness" boundary needs an explicit test/guard or it will accrete logic.
  - No statement of clock source/monotonicity for `at`/`duration_ms` (NTP steps, cross-process skew) yet total time is derived from them.
NIT:
  - `gate_decide` vs `gate_decisions` naming; `set_status(completed)` trigger ordering versus `delivery` event ordering should be spelled into the canonical stage sequence diagram.
  - Guardrail 8 (needs_api) not explicitly answered as "no" in the design; state it to close the checklist.
  - Legacy backfill out-of-scope is fine, but note the show CLI behavior for items with zero/partial trails (`not captured` semantics) for consistency.
SUMMARY:
  - Sound, reversible, tooling-only design that fits the standards, but it is under-specified exactly where integrity matters: write-failure signaling, atomic/locked seq allocation, stage ownership, and the check's diff scoping.
  - Top risks: gate can pass on a fake/garbled trail, and the failure event path is self-referential.
  - Approve only after the failure-sink, locking/atomicity, stage-ownership, and diff-scoping rules are stated and covered by fail-able tests.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=f041f37b198a
BLOCKER:
  - No `scripts/dev/execution_trail.py` exists; `core/execution_trail.py` is the full 296-line implementation, not the AC-specified thin adapter — this required editing the reviewed `language-rule.json` governance config to exempt new shipped Python, violating A6/ADR-0007 ("new shipped logic -> Go", root changes are a governance change).
  - The completion gate never inspects `engineering/trails/_failures.jsonl` nor fails on a structured `execution_trail_write_failed` event; AC "a trail write failure ... the completion gate fails" is unimplemented.
  - `core/backlog.py` `set_status`/`set_delivery` swallow trail failures with a plain `print` warning (no structured event, no failure sink), so a lost `completion`/`delivery` record is silently accepted — `completion` is not in `REQUIRED_AT_COMPLETION`, so the gate cannot catch it.
MAJOR:
  - `order_problems` validates only `design_review<gate1` and `diff_review<gate2`; AC requires all pre-merge stages missing **or out of order** — e.g. `tests` before `implementation` or `precheck` before `tests` passes the gate.
  - Broken error paths: `gate0_check.py` calls `execution_trail.write_failure(...)` but only `trail` is imported → `NameError` escapes the handler and crashes the gate; `precheck._record_trail`'s `except` references `trail` which may be unimported if the import itself failed → same masking.
  - No stale-lock recovery: a crash between `_lock` and `unlink` leaves a permanent `.lock`; every subsequent write for that item times out after 10s — a self-inflicted permanent write DoS with no owner or cleanup.
  - Non-idempotent appends: `gate0_check` re-records `planning`/`gate0` and `precheck` re-records `code_review`/`tests`/`precheck` on every run → unbounded growth toward `MAX_EVENTS` and last-wins `_stage_events` masking earlier failures; `planning` is always recorded `"pass"` regardless of gate0 problems.
  - `execution_trail_check` runs twice in precheck (via `_GATES` tier `"post"` and the explicit post-runner invocation) — the `_GATES` copy can execute before the runner writes `tests`/`precheck`, defeating the stated ordering guarantee.
  - Brittle private coupling: the check imports `gate2_completion_check` internals (`g2.ar._get_item`, `g2._git`, `g2.transitions`) and `architect_review.py` shells out a 60s subprocess from `show`; either upstream refactor silently breaks the gate/CLI.
MINOR:
  - `usage_totals` skips events with empty `usage` instead of counting them as `not_captured`, so AC "'not captured' when unavailable" under-reports; `cost_usd` is never populated by any writer, so cost columns are always 0.
  - `_LAST_USAGE` is a module-global in `architect_review.py`: concurrent or sequential reviews in one process misattribute token usage to the wrong stage/evidence.
  - Only `summary`/`actor` are redacted; `refs` and `tests` pass through unredacted (e.g. commit lists, branch names, commands with env values).
  - `--sha` path calls `gate_view_sha(...)`, which is not introduced in this diff — verify it exists, else `NameError` on the documented history-render path.
  - `gate_decisions` records stage `f"gate{gate}"` — verify `gate` is always `"1"`/`"2"`; any `"1.5"`/`"2.5"` value raises and drops the decision from the trail.
  - `ci-cd-gates.json` gate `area: ["data/backlog"]` does not cover `engineering/trails/**`, so trail-only changes may not trigger the gate.
  - Store `allow` entry `"_failures.jsonl"` is a bare glob matching any path in the repo, not just `engineering/trails/_failures.jsonl`.
  - Self-test gaps: no test for the full-ordering rule, for `evaluate()`/`main()`, or for the write-failure→gate-fails path (the headline AC behavior).
NIT:
  - `language-rule.json` was fully reformatted from compact to expanded arrays, burying the one real change in a large governance-config diff.
  - Dead `if a.report: continue` in `gate0_check` (the loop is after `return` on `a.report`); duplicate `import json` inside `precheck._record_trail`'s `except`; duplicate `from core import backlog` in `next_item`.
  - `docs/REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md` names `scripts/dev/execution_trail.py` as owner and `gate_decisions`/`precheck` writers that don't match the code (`gate_decide`, `implementation/code_review` attributed to precheck only).
SUMMARY:
  - Solid foundations (append-only store, atomic `os.replace`, per-item lock, secret redaction, tests, gate wiring), but the item does not meet its AC: the required thin-adapter split is inverted into new shipped Python plus a governance-config exemption, and the mandated write-failure→completion-gate-fails behavior is entirely absent.
  - The ordering check is only a partial implementation of "out of order", and several failure paths crash with `NameError` instead of emitting the structured event.
  - Top risks: silent trail loss at completion/delivery, non-idempotent unbounded growth, permanent lockout after a crash, and language-rule baseline erosion.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

No dedupe, rotation, or prune strategy for an "unbounded" retention store.

Combined with `write_failure`'s bare `except Exception: pass`, failure evidence can also be silently lost.

  - Lock design can break monotonic seq: 10s acquire timeout vs 60s stale-break means a live writer holding >10s makes peers fail (surfacing as completion-blocking write failures), while a stale break at 60s can steal a live lock and allow duplicate seq. No fsync; crash between `os.replace` and lock unlink is only recovered after 60s.
  - Language-rule governance change bundled silently: `core/execution_trail.py` (new shipped logic under `shipped_roots`) is self-added to `allow_new_python` in the same diff, though the config itself states root/allowlist changes are a governed change — no evidence of the required approval, and the logic is substantive (store, locking, redaction, CLI), not a thin adapter.

  - `execution_trail_check` reaches into `g2.ar._get_item` (private internals of another gate) — brittle coupling; extract a shared accessor.
  - No test asserts the check *fails* on out-of-order stages, on `_failures.jsonl` entries, or exercises the precheck wiring, though the AC requires the gate be self-tested; only happy/missing-path cases are covered.
NIT:
